title: Rational module coactions over a commutative base ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $G$ an affine group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Use its canonical coordinate Hopf algebra $C_G=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra] and tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For an arbitrary $A$-module $V$, a rational coaction is an $A$-linear map $\rho:V\to V\otimes_A C_G$ satisfying $(1\otimes\varepsilon)\rho=1$ and $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$, under the canonical unit and associativity identifications; this is the counital coassociative right coordinate coaction of [def-sfb-affine-group-distribution-calculus], taken over the commutative base ring $A$. Define $V^G=\ker(\rho-(v\mapsto v\otimes1))$. A linear map $f:V\to W$ is equivariant when $(f\otimes1)\rho_V=\rho_W f$. For a homomorphism $j:H\to G$ of affine group schemes, the canonical coordinate map $j^*:C_G\to C_H$ is pullback of global functions, with its $A$-algebra structure from the over-base square. Restriction of a coaction is $(1\otimes j^*)\rho$; when $j$ is a quotient map this is called inflation. No module finiteness or flatness and no smoothness or reducedness condition on the groups is imposed.
